'''Bernice Black Durand''' (28 December 1942 - 7 February 2022) was an American particle physicist and emeritus Professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. She was also the emeritus Vice Provost for Diversity and Climate.

== Early life and education ==
Durand was born in [[Clarion, Iowa]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://plaza.las.iastate.edu/directory/bernice-black-durand/|title=Bernice Black Durand -|website=Plaza of Heroines|language=en|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> Her father studied [[mechanical engineering]] at [[Iowa State University]] and [[Harvard University]], and joined the [[United States Army Corps of Engineers]].<ref name="iastate.academicworks.com">{{Cite web|url=https://iastate.academicworks.com/opportunities/2140|title=Bernice Black Durand Undergraduate Research Scholarship - Iowa State University Scholarships|website=iastate.academicworks.com|language=en|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She grew up in [[Ames, Iowa|Ames]] and attended [[Radcliffe College]], but never finished her course.<ref name=":0" /> She eventually completed her bachelor's degree from [[Iowa State University]] in 1965.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physastro.iastate.edu/alumni/bio/bio-bdurand|title=Biography: Prof. Bernice Durand {{!}} Department of Physics & Astronomy|website=www.physastro.iastate.edu|language=en-us|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She earned her PhD with a dissertation titled ''A point and local position operator,'' in 1971.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hep.wisc.edu/~bdurand/Vitae/vitae.html|title=VITAE|last=|first=|date=|website=WISC|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Durand|first=Bernice Black|title=A point and local position operator|date=1971|publisher=Iowa State University|url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/rtd/4876/|doi=10.31274/rtd-180813-3680|language=en|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/tree.php?pid=547602|title=Physics Tree - Bernice Black Durand Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She was a member of [[Sigma Delta Epsilon]]. From 1992 she has endowed an undergraduate research scholarship at [[Iowa State University]], which provides financial support for a member of an under-represented group to complete a summer project.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="iastate.academicworks.com"/> Durand died on February 7, 2022, from complications with Alzheimer's Disease.<ref name=":3" />

== Research and career ==
Durand was appointed to the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1970.<ref name=":1" /> She was a much celebrated teacher, teaching all levels at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. She appeared in the [[Aspen Center for Physics]] video series.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mc.grassrootstv.org/cablecast/public/Show.aspx?ChannelID=1&ShowID=1375|title=Video On-Demand|website=mc.grassrootstv.org|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She worked on the [[SVZ sum rules|SVZ]] method to calculate [[hadron]]ic masses as well as heavy-quark systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Durand|first1=Bernice|last2=Durand|first2=Loyal|date=1981-03-01|title=Duality for heavy-quark systems|journal=Physical Review D|volume=23|issue=5|pages=1092–1102|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1092|bibcode=1981PhRvD..23.1092D}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1983-05-05|title=The SVZ method: Why it works and why it fails|journal=Physics Letters B|language=en|volume=124|issue=5|pages=410–414|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)91485-5|issn=0370-2693|last1=Durand|first1=Bernice|last2=Whitenton|first2=James B.|last3=Durand|first3=L.|bibcode=1983PhLB..124..410D}}</ref> During her career she was a visiting scientist in several national facilities. She worked at the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] in 1973, 1982 and 1984.<ref name=":1" /> She also worked at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/bernice-durand|title=Bernice Durand|work=Institute for Advanced Study|access-date=2018-09-19|language=en}}</ref> In 1994, [[Iowa State University]] endowed a brick in the [[Iowa State University]] ''Plaza of Heroines''.<ref name=":0" />

Durand has been involved in several initiatives to improve diversity amongst the faculty and student population at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hep.wisc.edu/~bdurand/Vitae/Bs_bio.html|title=Associate Vice Chancellor Emerita for Diversity and Climate|last=|first=|date=|website=WISC|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She directed an [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] grant that promoted equity and career flexibility for all academic staff.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wisconsin.edu/news/archive/uw-system-receives-grant-to-study-workplace-enhancement/|title=UW System receives grant to study workplace enhancement|date=2003-07-30|work=News|access-date=2018-09-19|language=en-US}}</ref> She was a founder of the [[National Science Foundation]] Women in Science and Engineering Leadership Institute.<ref name=":2" /> She served on the Committee on the Status of Women in Physics.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.aspenpublicradio.org/people/bernice-durand|title=Bernice Durand|access-date=2018-09-19|language=en}}</ref> Her efforts were widely appreciated; in 2002 she received the Chancellor's Recognition Award for Outstanding Leadership and the Faculty and Staff Recognition Award from the Wisconsin Alumni Association's Cabinet 99.<ref name=":2" /> In her final five years at UW Madison, Durand was appointed the first Vice Provost for Diversity and Climate, in charge of all university climate and diversity programs. A Faculty Fellowship in physics has since been established in her honor.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Obituary: Bernice Durand |url=https://www.aspentimes.com/obituaries/obituary-bernice-durand/ |access-date=2022-03-15 |website=www.aspentimes.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Durand endorsed [[Barack Obama]] in the [[United States elections, 2008|2008 United States presidential election]].<ref>{{Citation|last=AVoteForScience|title=Bernice Durand Endorses Barack Obama|date=2008-10-30|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqfLDaeXC48|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref> She campaigned for the democratic candidate, working with over thirty scientists to publish articles and letters in newspapers across the country.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Science|first=American Association for the Advancement of|date=2008-10-31|title=News this Week|url=http://science.sciencemag.org/content/322/5902/news-summaries|journal=Science|language=en|volume=322|issue=5902|pages=658–9|issn=0036-8075|pmid=18974320|doi=10.1126/science.322.5902.658|s2cid=206582810 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
